title: Time Series & Forecasting
tagline: Predict what happens next: trend, seasonality, ARIMA, boosted trees, deep models, and today's pretrained forecasting models.
prereqs: Machine Learning. Deep Learning helps for the later steps.

steps.title: Stationarity
steps.why: Why most classical models need a steady mean and variance.

steps.title: Trend, seasonality, and decomposition
steps.why: Split a series into parts you can reason about.

steps.title: Exponential smoothing and Holt-Winters
steps.why: A strong baseline that handles trend and seasons.

steps.title: ARIMA
steps.why: Autoregression, differencing, and moving averages in one model.

steps.title: Cross-validation for time series
steps.why: Validate forward in time so you never peek at the future.

steps.title: Forecasting with XGBoost
steps.why: Lag and calendar features with gradient-boosted trees.

steps.title: LSTM forecasting
steps.why: A first neural forecaster, with its limits shown clearly.

steps.title: Temporal Fusion Transformer
steps.why: Multi-horizon forecasts with attention and interpretable features.

steps.title: Time series foundation models
steps.why: Why pretrained forecasters can work zero-shot.

steps.title: Chronos: pretrained forecasting
steps.why: Forecast with a pretrained model and read its probabilistic output.

steps.title: Anomaly detection basics
steps.why: Spot unusual points with robust statistics and isolation forests.

projects: Forecast daily demand for one public dataset with seasonal-naive, ARIMA, and XGBoost baselines, scored with rolling-origin validation.
Compare a pretrained model such as Chronos with your best classical model on three series.
Build an anomaly detector for sensor or server data using z-scores and Isolation Forest, and plot its alerts.
